candidateDecisions.label: Neurobiology and neurological disease
candidateDecisions.reason: Comparative neurobiology, perception and higher brain functions offer a credible direction. They already strengthen the closest option, while a separate route would cover less of the degree’s broader experimental and quantitative identity than the retained options.

stoppingDecision.assessment: Three UCR options provide distinct study in disease mechanisms, prevention and quantitative methods. The quantitative option develops transferable methods for biomedical questions. The dedicated omics and research placement remain specific to the UvA curriculum.

analysis: The closest option moves from cells and evolutionary genetics to physiology, biochemistry and anatomy, then lab techniques, immunity, pathology and pharmacology. The lab includes PCR, culture, DNA and proteins, without covering a full wet-lab omics or live-cell microscopy sequence. Quantitative and ethical courses support research. The population option builds from epidemiology and human biology into qualitative methods, policy, health behaviour and intervention evidence. Public economics offers public goods and policy tools, not a dedicated health-financing course. The quantitative option uses general image processing, linear systems, numerical differential equations, statistics and machine learning alongside molecular and physiological study. It teaches transferable methods rather than a specialist genomics or personalised-treatment sequence. Description-only Perception & Action examines sensory and motor mechanisms and supports the closest option. Comparative neurobiology, perception and cognition could support a fourth direction, but their strongest contributions already appear within the closest programme. Each retained option has a separate question and course spine. Removed inaccurate VU notes, shifted imaging into an offered spring term and improved the laboratory sequence. Only the nine positive rows with identifiable shared subject matter remain paired. The research placement and optional UCR independent research remain clearly distinct.
